 MACC hands over wanted Chinese national to embassy
 20-Nov-2026, 09:23 20 Nov 2026, 09:23 FMT Reporters Share He is suspected of bribing enforcement officers to avoid action in connection with fraud and money laundering cases.
 MACC referred the suspect’s case to the immigration department and the Chinese embassy before handing him over to the embassy yesterday for further action. 
 PUTRAJAYA : The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has handed over a Chinese national wanted by his country’s authorities to the Chinese embassy in Kuala Lumpur. 
 An MACC source said the man was suspected of bribing enforcement officers to avoid action in connection with fraud and money laundering cases.
 The man, in his 50s and self-employed, was arrested on Nov 17 at about 9pm when he went to give a statement at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
 Checks found that he was wanted by China’s National Commission of Supervision (NCS), the country’s highest state supervisory and anti-corruption authority, and his passport had been cancelled by the Chinese government.
 MACC subsequently referred the case to the immigration department and the Chinese embassy before handing him over to the embassy yesterday for further action.
 MACC chief commissioner Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted.
 MACC and NCS agreed yesterday to strengthen cooperation in corruption investigations and enforcement.
 The collaboration was discussed during a courtesy visit by an NCS delegation, led by its vice-chairman Sun Xinyang, to the MACC headquarters.
 In a Facebook post, Halim said cooperation between the two agencies had continued growing since they signed a memorandum of understanding on Oct 17, 2023.
 He said the five-year agreement, which is subject to automatic renewal, provided an important framework for strengthening joint efforts to combat corruption.
 “The meeting will open up further opportunities for cooperation between the two institutions, particularly through the sharing of expertise and experience to strengthen the effectiveness of corruption prevention and enforcement efforts,” he said.
